question.text: A car travels at $1\,000$ meters per minute. In kilometers, how far will the car travel in one hour?
question.explanation:
We are given the units $\dfrac{\textrm{m}}{\textrm{min}},$ and we want to convert this into $\dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{hour}}.$ We're converting two units instead of just one, so we're going to have to multiply by two conversion factors: \[ \dfrac{\textrm{m}}{\textrm{min}} \cdot \, \dfrac{?}{?} \cdot \, \dfrac{?}{?} = \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{hour}} \]

One of the conversion factors should change $\textrm{m}$ to $\textrm{km}.$ \[ \dfrac{\cancel{\textrm{m}} }{\textrm{min}} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\cancel{\textrm{m}} } \cdot \, \dfrac{?}{?} = \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{hour}} \]

The other conversion factor should change $\textrm{min}$ into $\textrm{hour}.$ \[ \dfrac{\cancel{\textrm{m}} }{ \cancel{\textrm{min}} }\cdot \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\cancel{\textrm{m}} } \cdot \dfrac{ \cancel{\textrm{min}} }{ \textrm{hour} } = \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{hour}} \]

So, our conversion formula is \[ \dfrac{\textrm{m}}{\textrm{min}} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{m}} \cdot \dfrac{ \textrm{min}}{ \textrm{hour} } = \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{hour}}. \]

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

  • The rate given in the problem statement is $1\,000 \, \dfrac{\textrm{m}}{\textrm{min}}.$
  • There are $1\,000$ meters per kilometer, therefore, there are $\dfrac{1}{1\,000}$ kilometers per meter.
  • There are $60$ minutes in one hour.

Applying our conversion formula, we have \begin{align} \require{cancel} 1000 \,\dfrac{\textrm{m}}{\textrm{min}}&= 1000 \,\dfrac{\textrm{m}}{\textrm{min}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{1\,000}\,\dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{m}} \cdot 60 \,\dfrac{\textrm{min}}{\textrm{hour}} \\[5pt] &= 1000 \cdot \dfrac{1}{1\,000} \cdot 60 \left(\dfrac{\cancel{\textrm{m}}}{\cancel{\textrm{min}}} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\cancel{\textrm{m}}} \cdot \dfrac{\cancel{\textrm{min}}}{\textrm{hour}} \right)\\[5pt] &= 60\,\dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{hour}}. \end{align}

Consequently, a speed of $1\,000$ meters per minute is equivalent to $60$ kilometers per hour. Thus, the car will travel $60$ kilometers in one hour.

example.title: Performing a Unit Conversion: Converting a Numerator and a Denominator

question.text: At the start of a launch, a space rocket consumes about $150$ kilograms of fuel per second. How much fuel does it consume per minute?
question.explanation:
We are given the units $\dfrac{\textrm{kg}}{\textrm{s}},$ and we want to convert this into $\dfrac{\textrm{kg}}{\textrm{min}}.$ To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us:

\[ \dfrac{\textrm{kg}}{\textrm{s}}\cdot\, \dfrac{?}{?} = \dfrac{\textrm{kg}}{\textrm{min}} \]

We want to replace $\textrm{s}$ with $\textrm{min}.$ To get rid of $\textrm{s},$ we can put $\textrm{s}$ in the numerator so that it cancels out. To introduce $\textrm{min},$ we can put $\textrm{min}$ in the denominator.

\[ \require{cancel} \dfrac{\textrm{kg} }{ \cancel{\textrm{s}}}\cdot \dfrac{ \cancel{ \textrm{s} } }{ \textrm{min} } = \dfrac{\textrm{kg}}{\textrm{min}} \]

So, our conversion formula is

\[ \require{cancel} \dfrac{\textrm{kg} }{ \textrm{s}}\cdot \dfrac{ \textrm{s} }{ \textrm{min} } = \dfrac{\textrm{kg}}{\textrm{min}}. \]

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

  • The rate given in the problem statement is $150 \, \dfrac{\textrm{kg}}{\textrm{s}}.$
  • There are $60$ seconds per minute.

Applying our conversion formula, we have \begin{align} \require{cancel} 150 \, \dfrac{\textrm{kg}}{\textrm{s}} &= 150 \, \dfrac{\textrm{kg}}{\textrm{s}}\cdot 60 \,\dfrac{\textrm{s}}{\textrm{min}} \\[5pt] &= \left( 150 \cdot 60 \right) \, \dfrac{\textrm{kg}} { \cancel{\textrm{s}} }\cdot \dfrac{ \cancel{\textrm{s}}}{\textrm{min}} \\[5pt] &= 9\,000 \,\dfrac{\textrm{kg}}{\textrm{min}}. \end{align}

Thus, the space rocket consumes $9\,000$ kilograms per minute.

example.title: Performing a Unit Conversion: Converting a Denominator

question.text: The cheetah is considered the fastest land animal. It can achieve a speed of $120$ kilometers per hour. What is this speed in kilometers per minute?
question.explanation:
We are given the units $\dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{h}},$ and we want to convert this into $\dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{min}}.$ To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us:

\[ \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{h}}\cdot\, \dfrac{?}{?} = \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{min}} \]

We want to replace $\textrm{h}$ with $\textrm{min}.$ To get rid of $\textrm{h},$ we can put $\textrm{h}$ in the numerator so that it cancels out. To introduce $\textrm{min},$ we can put $\textrm{min}$ in the denominator.

\[ \require{cancel} \dfrac{\textrm{km} }{ \cancel{\textrm{h}}}\cdot \dfrac{ \cancel{ \textrm{h} } }{ \textrm{min} } = \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{min}} \]

So, our conversion formula is

\[ \dfrac{\textrm{km} }{\textrm{h}}\cdot \dfrac{ \textrm{h} }{ \textrm{min} } = \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{min}} . \]

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

  • The rate given in the problem statement is $120 \, \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{h}}.$
  • There are $60$ minutes per hour. Taking the reciprocal, there are $\dfrac{1}{60}$ hours per minute.

Applying our conversion formula, we have \begin{align} \require{cancel} 120 \, \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{h}} &= 120 \, \dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{h}}\cdot \dfrac{1}{60} \,\dfrac{\textrm{h}}{\textrm{min}} \\[5pt] &= \left( 120 \cdot \dfrac{1}{60} \right) \, \dfrac{\textrm{km}} { \cancel{\textrm{h}} }\cdot \dfrac{ \cancel{\textrm{h}}}{\textrm{min}} \\[5pt] &= 2 \,\dfrac{\textrm{km}}{\textrm{min}}. \end{align}

Thus, the cheetah can run at a speed $2 \,\textrm{km}/\textrm{min}.$
